html:
The Asante Empire was an Akan state in the forest of what is now Ghana, from 1701 to 1902, ruled by a king called the Asantehene from Kumasi. At its height it covered most of modern Ghana and parts of Ivory Coast and Togo.

Around 1700 the king Osei Tutu and his priest Okomfo Anokye united several Akan states. Tradition says Anokye called the Golden Stool down from the sky; it holds the soul of the nation and no one sits on it. In 1701 the Asante defeated Denkyira, the state they had paid tribute to.

The empire was rich in gold. It sold kola nuts to the north and captives to Europeans on the coast for the Atlantic slave trade. Great roads ran out from Kumasi, and the state kept a trained civil service and messengers.

When Britain banned the slave trade in 1807, Asante lost a major export, and it clashed with the British on the coast. The Anglo-Asante wars ran through the 1800s:

  • 1824: Asante forces killed the British governor Charles MacCarthy.
  • 1874: a British army burned Kumasi.
  • 1896: the British exiled King Prempeh I.
  • 1900: when the British governor demanded the Golden Stool, Queen Mother Yaa Asantewaa led a last war.

Britain annexed Asante in 1902. The Asantehene still reigns as a traditional king.
